title: First introductions
goal: Greet people, give your given name and surname, say where you're from and what you do, and ask yes/no questions — all with a single verb: 是.
bekal: give your name with 叫 and your surname with 姓
ask questions with 吗 and bounce a question back with 呢

dialogs.title: 对话 1 — Meeting in class
dialogs.intro: Andi, a teacher from Jakarta, meets Wang Li on his first day in Beijing. Notice that the whole conversation runs on just one verb.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.literal: you — good.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.literal: you — good. I — am-called — Andi.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: My surname is Wang, my name is Wang Li.
lines.literal: I — am-surnamed — Wang, am-called — Wang Li.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.literal: know — you — (support) — happy.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [我|Wǒ][也|yě][很|hěn][高兴|gāoxìng]。[你是|Nǐ shì][哪国人|nǎ guó rén]？
lines.id: Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
lines.literal: I — also — (support) — happy. you — are — which — country — person.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我是|Wǒ shì][印尼人|Yìnní rén]。[你呢|Nǐ ne]？
lines.literal: I — am — Indonesia — person. you — (and)?

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [我是|Wǒ shì][中国人|Zhōngguó rén]。[你是|Nǐ shì][学生|xuésheng][吗|ma]？
lines.id: I'm Chinese. Are you a student?
lines.literal: I — am — China — person. you — are — student — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [不是|Bú shì]，[我是|wǒ shì][老师|lǎoshī]。[你|Nǐ][也是|yě shì][老师|lǎoshī][吗|ma]？
lines.id: No, I'm a teacher. Are you a teacher too?
lines.literal: not — am, I — am — teacher. you — also — are — teacher — (question).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [我|Wǒ][不是|bú shì][老师|lǎoshī]，[我是|wǒ shì][学生|xuésheng]。
lines.id: I'm not a teacher, I'm a student.
lines.literal: I — not — am — teacher, I — am — student.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.literal: you — 's — name — (support) — good-to-hear.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.literal: thanks. again — see.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.literal: again — see.

notes: **[你好|Nǐ hǎo] literally means “you good”** — and it is a **statement**, not a question. It works any time, with anyone, like “hello”. To ask how someone is, you say [你好吗|Nǐ hǎo ma]？ with 吗 at the end.

**[姓|xìng] is only for surnames, [叫|jiào] is for names.** [我姓王|Wǒ xìng Wáng] = my surname is Wang. [我叫王丽|Wǒ jiào Wáng Lì] = my name is Wang Li. ⚠️ Learners often say 我姓安迪 for their first name — which sounds like “my surname is Andi”. If in doubt, use 叫; it is almost always right.

**Chinese names run the other way from English: surname first, then given name.** 王丽 = surname 王, given name 丽. The same goes for 毛泽东 and 习近平 — the first syllable is the surname. Chinese surnames are almost always one syllable.
**[呢|ne] bounces a question back without repeating it.** After someone asks you something, just answer and add [你呢|Nǐ ne]？ — “and you?” It saves a whole sentence and sounds very natural.

**⚠️ 不 changes tone before a fourth tone.** On its own, 不 is *bù* (tone 4), but [不是|bú shì] is said *bú* (tone 2) because 是 is also a fourth tone. The same happens in [不去|bú qù], [不要|bú yào], [不错|bú cuò]. The character stays 不.
**⚠️ [也|yě] “also” goes before the verb, never at the end of the sentence.** [我也是老师|Wǒ yě shì lǎoshī] = I'm a teacher too. “I am teacher too” word order doesn't exist in Mandarin.
**[很|hěn] in [很高兴|hěn gāoxìng] doesn't mean “very”.** It's a required support word placed before adjectives. We'll sort this out fully in Unit 8 — for now, just learn the pair as a unit.

grammars.title: 是 — one verb is enough for this whole unit
body: [是|shì] links two **nouns**: A 是 B means “A is B”. Mandarin verbs never change form, so 是 is exactly the same for I, you, he, we, and they — no *am / is / are* juggling as in English.

head: Person
Mandarin
Example
rows: [我是老师|Wǒ shì lǎoshī]。 I'm a teacher.
[你是学生|Nǐ shì xuésheng]。 You're a student.
[您是王先生|Nín shì Wáng xiānsheng]？ Are you Mr. Wang?
[他是医生|Tā shì yīshēng]。 He's a doctor.
[她是我朋友|Tā shì wǒ péngyou]。 She's my friend.
[我们是印尼人|Wǒmen shì Yìnní rén]。 We're Indonesian.
[你们是学生吗|Nǐmen shì xuésheng ma]？
[他们是中国人|Tāmen shì Zhōngguó rén]。

head: Form
Pattern
Example
rows: [我不是中国人|Wǒ bú shì Zhōngguó rén]。

after: ⚠️ **是 is never used with adjectives.** “I'm busy” is **not** 我是忙 but [我很忙|Wǒ hěn máng]. This is the number-one mistake English speakers make, because English says “I *am* busy” — and it lasts for years if it isn't pulled out now. Remember: 是 only links **noun to noun**.

grammars.title: Three ways to ask a question in Mandarin
body: Mandarin never flips the word order to ask a question. A question has **exactly the same** word order as a statement — only one small word changes.

head: Method
How
Example
Answer
rows: Add [吗|ma] to the end of a statement
Put the question word exactly where the answer goes
[你是哪国人|Nǐ shì nǎ guó rén]？
Noun + [呢|ne] — bounces the last question back

after: ⚠️ **Mandarin question words don't move to the front.** English says “**who** is he?”; Mandarin says [他是谁|Tā shì shéi]？ — literally “he is who”. Easy check: build the answer sentence first, then swap the part you don't know for a question word. Not a single word needs to move.
⚠️ 吗 and a question word **can't be used together**. [你是谁吗|Nǐ shì shéi ma]？ is wrong — just [你是谁|Nǐ shì shéi]？

dialogs.title: 对话 2 — Introducing a third person
dialogs.intro: That afternoon Wang Li introduces Andi to her friend. Watch for 这 and 那 — two words you'll use hundreds of times from the next unit on.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [安迪|Āndí]，[这是|zhè shì][我|wǒ][朋友|péngyou][李明|Lǐ Míng]。
lines.id: Andi, this is my friend, Li Ming.
lines.literal: Andi, this — is — I — friend — Li Ming.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.literal: you — good, Li Ming.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.literal: you — good. you — are-called — what — name.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我|Wǒ][叫|jiào][安迪|Āndí]。[我是|Wǒ shì][印尼人|Yìnní rén]。
lines.id: My name is Andi. I'm Indonesian.
lines.literal: I — am-called — Andi. I — am — Indonesia — person.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [印尼|Yìnní]？[太好了|Tài hǎo le]！[我|Wǒ][很|hěn][喜欢|xǐhuan][巴厘岛|Bālí Dǎo]。
lines.id: Indonesia? That's great! I love Bali.
lines.literal: Indonesia. too — good — (change). I — (support) — like — Bali.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [真的|Zhēn de][吗|ma]？[你|Nǐ][去过|qù guo][印尼|Yìnní][吗|ma]？
lines.id: Really? Have you been to Indonesia?
lines.literal: real — (of) — (question). you — go — ever — Indonesia — (question).

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.literal: go — ever, two — times. that — is — who.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: That's my colleague. He's a teacher too.
lines.literal: that — is — I — colleague. he — also — is — teacher.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [你们|Nǐmen][都|dōu][是|shì][老师|lǎoshī]？[太好了|Tài hǎo le]！
lines.literal: you-all — all — are — teacher. too — good — (change).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.literal: correct. tomorrow — see.

notes: **[这|zhè] = this, [那|nà] = that.** Both are used for things and for people. Introducing someone always uses 这 — [这是我朋友|Zhè shì wǒ péngyou], literally “this is my friend”, just as in English.
**[什么|shénme] = what.** Notice where it sits: [你叫什么名字|Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi]？ — literally “you are-called what name”. It stands exactly where the answer will stand.

**[太好了|Tài hǎo le] = “that's great!”.** The pattern [太|tài] + adjective + [了|le] is used for anything that goes over the top: [太贵了|tài guì le] way too expensive, [太累了|tài lèi le] so tired. It's one of the most common patterns in everyday conversation.
**[都|dōu] = “all/both”, and it always comes after the subject, before the verb.** [我们都是老师|Wǒmen dōu shì lǎoshī] = we're all teachers. ⚠️ 都 can never go at the start of the sentence like “all we …”.
**[去过|qù guo] = have been (to).** We'll cover 过 fully in Unit 10; for now, just recognize that 过 means “have ever, at least once”.
**[明天见|Míngtiān jiàn] = see you tomorrow.** The pattern is time + 见: [回头见|huítóu jiàn] see you later, [下周见|xiàzhōu jiàn] see you next week. Much warmer than the flat 再见.

grammars.title: 这 and 那 — pointing things out

head: Mandarin
Meaning
Example
rows: [这是我的书|Zhè shì wǒ de shū]。
[那是他的车|Nà shì tā de chē]。

after: ⚠️ Look closely: [那|nà] “that” and [哪|nǎ] “which” differ only in tone and one small part on the left of the character (口). This is the pair beginners mix up most. How to tell them apart: the one that **asks** has a mouth 口 in front.

blocks.text: 你好 is always correct, but Chinese people rarely use it with people they already know. The greetings below make you sound natural, not like a textbook.

head: Greeting
When to use it
Natural reply
rows: Any time, especially with new people
To a whole group at once
Morning. Just 早 is enough among friends
Asking how someone you know is doing
“How have you been lately?” — used far more often
Friendly greeting, literally “eaten yet?” — not an invitation to eat

head: Saying goodbye
Nuance
rows: Casual, from “bye bye”, very common among young people
Said by the **host** to a guest who is leaving — literally “walk slowly”

blocks.title: Manners to know from day one
items: **[谢谢|Xièxie]** — thank you. The reply is [不客气|Bú kèqi] or [不用谢|Bú yòng xiè].
**[对不起|Duìbuqǐ]** — sorry, for real mistakes. The reply is [没关系|Méi guānxi] or [没事儿|Méi shìr].
**[不好意思|Bù hǎoyìsi]** — “excuse me, sorry” for small things: cutting in, being five minutes late, putting someone out. Used far more often than 对不起.
**[请问|Qǐngwèn]** — “may I ask”. Always put it before a question to a stranger. This one word changes the whole impression of your sentence.
⚠️ Chinese people say 谢谢 to family and close friends much less than English speakers do. Thanking a close friend too much actually feels distancing.

blocks.text: Your name will be the first thing you say in every introduction for as long as you speak Mandarin. These three patterns cover every situation.

head: Pattern
Register
Example
rows: Formal and a bit stiff; for forms or officials
[我的名字是安迪|Wǒ de míngzi shì Āndí]。
**Asking someone's surname politely** — literally “your honorable surname?”
[免贵姓王|Miǎn guì xìng Wáng]。 / [我姓王|Wǒ xìng Wáng]。
[你叫什么名字|Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi]？

blocks.text: The pattern is very regular: country name + [人|rén] = its people, country name + [语|yǔ] or [文|wén] = its language. Once you know the country, the other two words come free.

blocks.title: The jobs people ask about most
items: [学生|xuésheng] student · [老师|lǎoshī] teacher · [医生|yīshēng] doctor · [护士|hùshi] nurse
[工程师|gōngchéngshī] engineer · [律师|lǜshī] lawyer · [警察|jǐngchá] police officer · [司机|sījī] driver
[商人|shāngrén] businessperson · [服务员|fúwùyuán] waiter · [记者|jìzhě] journalist · [经理|jīnglǐ] manager
Asking: [你做什么工作|Nǐ zuò shénme gōngzuò]？ — “what work do you do?”
⚠️ You don't **have** to answer with 是: both [我是老师|Wǒ shì lǎoshī] (identity) and [我教书|Wǒ jiāo shū] (I teach) work. The first is more common.

items: [我是也老师|Wǒ shì yě lǎoshī]。
[谁是他|Shéi shì tā]？

answers: 是 — 不是 — 叫 — 叫 — 不是 — 是
谁 — 哪 — 什么 — 吗 — 呢
我 是 印尼 人 — 你 是 学生 吗 — 他 也 是 老师 — 这 是 我 朋友 — 我们 都 是 中国 人 — 认识 你 很 高兴
She isn't a doctor, she's a nurse. — Are you all Indonesian? — Who's that? — My surname is Wang, my name is Wang Li. — He isn't a teacher either.
Nǐ hǎo! Wǒ jiào Āndí. — Wǒ shì Yìnní rén. Nǐ ne? — Tā bú shì xuésheng. — Rènshi nǐ hěn gāoxìng. — Wǒmen dōu shì lǎoshī.
Wǒ yě shì lǎoshī. — Tā shì shéi? — Nǐ shì shéi? — Wǒ jiào Āndí. — Wǒmen dōu shì xuésheng.
wave: Five minutes before Unit 2: cover the meaning column in the vocabulary list, then introduce yourself out loud six times in a row — name, surname, where you're from, what you do — until it comes out without thinking. Introducing yourself is the one part of Mandarin you'll say for the rest of your life, and it has to be automatic.
